sources.name: Paystack: How NIBSS Instant Payment (NIP) powers Nigeria's digital economy
CBN Circular FPR/DIR/CIR/GEN/02/001: Introduction of Three-Tiered Know Your Customer Requirements
World Bank Fast Payments Toolkit: NIBSS Instant Payment NIP - Nigeria

entries.subject: nip_definition
entries.value_text: account-number based real-time electronic funds transfer platform with instant message delivery
entries.display: NIP is an account-number based, online real-time EFT platform where messages reach the receiving institution instantly
entries.quote: NIBSS Instant Payments (NIP) is an account number based, online real – time electronic fund transfer (EFT) platform where delivery of transaction messages from the Sending Institution to the Receiving Institution takes place instantly.
entries.notes: Page undated; effective_from is the capture date.

entries.subject: nip_participation
entries.display: All CBN licensed institutions have access to NIP
entries.quote: All CBN licensed institutions have access to this service by NIBSS for different use cases

entries.subject: nip_settlement_model
entries.display: NIP is a deferred net settlement system: funds are available to the beneficiary in real time before settlement, with 12 settlement sessions
entries.quote: NIBSS Instant Payment (NIP) is a Deferred Net Settlement (DNS) system where Funds are available online real-time in the beneficiary account before settlement.
entries.notes: The same FAQ answer states there are currently 12 settlement sessions on NIP.

entries.subject: nip_settlement_sessions
entries.display: NIP runs 12 settlement sessions per day for institutions
entries.quote: There are currently 12 sessions of settlement for institutions on the NIP service.

entries.subject: name_enquiry
entries.value_text: validates beneficiary account details by account number
entries.display: The Name Enquiry API lets the sending institution validate the beneficiary's details against the account number
entries.quote: Name Enquiry: enables the source institution validate the details of the beneficiary based on account number

entries.subject: nip_transaction_limit_basis
entries.value_text: set per CBN regulation and enforced per financial institution on the platform
entries.display: NIP's per-transaction maximum is set by CBN regulation and enforced on the platform per financial institution
entries.quote: The transaction limit on NIP is implemented in accordance with the CBN regulatory guidelines on the subject matter. The maximum allowable value per transaction per financial institution will be maintained on the platform but each participant is expected to also comply with regulation on transaction limit.
entries.notes: There is no single NIP-level amount; the cap is institutional and regulatory.

entries.subject: nip_launch_year
entries.display: NIBSS Instant Payment was launched in 2011
entries.quote: NIBSS Instant Payments (NIP) was launched in 2011 by NIBSS to electronically facilitate real-time bank transfers.
entries.notes: World Bank Fast Payments Toolkit also records year of implementation 2011 for NIP.

entries.subject: nuban_format
entries.display: NUBAN account numbers are a standardised 10-digit format directed by the CBN in 2011
entries.quote: the CBN directed all banks to adopt a standardized 10-digit account number format known as Nigeria Uniform Bank Account Number (NUBAN)

entries.subject: nip_direct_participants
entries.display: 315 institutions were direct participants in NIP at the time of the World Bank toolkit entry
entries.quote: Total number of system direct participants | 315
entries.notes: Toolkit page dated 2023; participant count moves, treat as a 2023 snapshot.

entries.subject: nip_non_bank_access
entries.value_text: no clearing access recorded for non-deposit-taking PSPs or third-party providers
entries.display: The World Bank toolkit records no clearing access for non-deposit-taking PSPs or third-party technology providers on NIP
entries.quote: Clearing access to non-deposit taking payment service providers |  | Clearing access to third-party/app/technology providers |  | Open access APIs | yes
entries.notes: The toolkit leaves both non-bank clearing-access fields blank while marking open access APIs as yes.

entries.subject: international_transfer_tier1
entries.display: Level 1 accounts cannot make international funds transfers

entries.subject: domestic_only_rail_access
entries.display: Level 2 accounts may only be used for funds transfers within Nigeria

notes: NIP has no single system-wide transaction ceiling; the cap is set by CBN regulation and enforced per institution.
